clue.text: Drunken men in the East not a problem for elephants

indicators.note: one set of letters sits inside the other, placed within it

parts.note: the continent often called the East

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A comic aside about tipsy men in the Orient, then an odd remark about elephants.
explanation.walkthrough: Elephants proverbially never forget, so memory loss is the one thing they are spared: the definition is a playful description, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverb says an elephant never forgets, so loss of memory is the condition such creatures famously escape.

clue.text: Performance of first part of play now showing

parts.note: a play is divided into acts, the first being Act I
a film or show that is running is on

explanation.surface: A theatre notice that the opening of a play is currently being performed.
explanation.definitionFit: An action is a deed or a performance of something, as in putting a plan into action.

clue.text: Tended to run over at speed, regularly

indicators.note: turned over, so the word that precedes it is read from its end back to its start
at regular intervals, so only every other letter of the following word is kept

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of speed

explanation.surface: Someone apparently rushed to help, driving fast with some regularity.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a patient is to look after or care for them, which is exactly what tending to someone means.

clue.text: I doubt belief system can be said to be healthy

definitions.text: I doubt belief system can be said to be healthy

parts.words: I doubt belief system can be said to be healthy
parts.note: surface: a speaker questions whether some creed or ideology does people any good
setter's reading: the whole sentence is itself an expression of doubting attitude, and belief system hints at the ending ism

explanation.surface: A doubter casts aspersions on the wholesomeness of some faith or ideology.
explanation.walkthrough: SCEPTICISM is the doubting attitude the speaker displays; belief system hints at the -ISM ending, and there is a sly nod to SEPTIC, the opposite of healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Voicing doubt that a creed is good for you is an instance of a questioning, doubting attitude towards claims.

clue.text: Detest serious assault on old republican

parts.note: actual bodily harm, a British criminal charge for a serious assault

explanation.surface: Revulsion at a violent attack on an elderly Republican politician.
explanation.walkthrough: ABH, actual bodily harm, is an offence in English law; in a down clue, on means placed on top of what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor something is to loathe or hate it intensely, the same strong feeling as detesting.

clue.text: Mobbed bird died after missing island

indicators.note: placed later in sequence, so the bird comes first and the rest follows
lacking something, so a letter is dropped from the word before

explanation.surface: A sad tale of a bird that perished after being parted from its island home.
explanation.definitionFit: A place that is mobbed is packed full of people, which is what crowded describes.

clue.text: Guardian could be no cheaper

indicators.note: suggests the letters might take another possible form when rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that a guardian's services are not going to cost any less.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperone accompanies and watches over a young person, acting as a protective guardian on outings.

clue.text: Chooses to stop being worried

indicators.note: worried in the sense of tugged and shaken about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone decides to give up fretting.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt is to make a selection or decision between alternatives, so opts means picks or selects.

clue.text: Interrupts usual routines to come back during children's game

indicators.note: happening within the span of something, so one part is set inside the other

parts.note: a game of knucklebones, also called jacks, in Britain

indicators.note: coming back means going the other way, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: being in a rut means stuck in a usual routine

explanation.surface: Playground games break up the normal daily routine when they return.
explanation.walkthrough: DIBS is an old British name for jacks, the game of tossing small stones or knucklebones.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb someone is to break in on what they are doing, which is to interrupt them.

clue.text: Condition resulting from bad sweets I chewed after losing wife and son

indicators.note: food that is chewed is mashed up, so the letters are jumbled
once things are lost they are gone, so some letters are removed

explanation.surface: A cautionary tale of a medical condition brought on by eating unhealthy sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one W and one S from the letters of bad sweets I before mixing them; the surface link of sugar and illness is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabetes is a chronic medical disorder of blood sugar, and condition is the general word for such an illness.

clue.text: Short of some computer services

indicators.note: only some of the letters are taken, a run lying within the words that follow

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A complaint that some IT services are lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A terse reply is brief and curt, so the word means short in the sense of clipped speech.

clue.text: This place makes dad better, without initially trying homeopathy

indicators.note: in its older sense of outside, so the first part goes around the second
at the start, so only the opening letter of each following word is used

parts.note: opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A retreat that restores father's wellbeing without any alternative remedies.
explanation.walkthrough: Without here means outside rather than lacking, which the surface hides well; the definition points back to the whole clue's description.
explanation.definitionFit: A health spa is a resort where people go to be restored, so this place is the venue the clue describes.

clue.text: Upset about change of direction by journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter is distressed at a U-turn in policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Upset in the sense of knocked over: an overturned vase or boat has been tipped up.

clue.text: Reportedly regretted being impolite

indicators.note: as reported by word of mouth, so the next word counts for how it sounds

explanation.surface: Someone is said to have felt sorry for their bad manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude and impolite are near-synonyms describing discourteous or offensive behaviour towards others.

clue.text: Still place soldiers next to a railway

parts.note: to station troops is to post them somewhere

explanation.surface: An order to keep troops posted beside a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stationary is not moving, motionless, which is the adjective sense of still.

clue.text: Form new board after company becomes prosperous

indicators.note: following on, so the firm's abbreviation comes in front of the rest
a new version of the word, so its letters are put in a fresh order

parts.note: a board is a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A business sets up a fresh board of directors and prospers.
explanation.definitionFit: Comfortable can mean well-off, having enough money to live without worry, close to prosperous.

clue.text: Intend joining women on hot French island for now

parts.note: to mean to do something is to intend it
abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Plans to go and join some women on a sunny French island, just for the time being.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanwhile means in the interim, during the time before something else happens, much like for the present.

clue.text: Worried about sweets

indicators.note: turned about, so the following word is read back to front

explanation.surface: Someone fretting over sugary treats.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain sweets is also a word for the dessert course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stressed means feeling anxious and under strain, which is close to being worried.

clue.text: Anti-cops riot makes headlines

indicators.note: a riot is wild disorder, so the letters run amok into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A riot against the police makes the front pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Captions are the titles printed above or below pictures and articles, like the headings called headlines.

clue.text: Clear partner tans unconventionally

indicators.note: not in the normal way, so the letters are set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: It is obvious that one's other half sunbathes in an unusual way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something transparent can be seen through, like clear glass or water.

clue.text: I'm the first figure to support South American singer

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporter stands underneath, so this part goes below the other

explanation.surface: A boast of being number one, backing the South.
explanation.walkthrough: Nina Simone was an American jazz and soul singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nina Simone was a celebrated American vocalist and pianist known as the High Priestess of Soul.

clue.text: Horrified at embracing terrible hags

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one part wraps around the other
something terrible is in a bad state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone recoils at the sight of being hugged by frightful old women.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means filled with shock and dismay, the same reaction as being horrified.

clue.text: Warms up unopened food

indicators.note: not opened, so the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: to heat something is to warm it up

explanation.surface: Reheating a meal still in its packet.
explanation.walkthrough: Eats is informal for food, as in a sign offering cheap eats.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is a colloquial plural noun for things to eat, an informal word for food.

clue.text: Consent to hang about drinking

indicators.note: around or surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to hang loosely and move to and fro
to allow is to consent to something

explanation.surface: Agreeing to loiter around while having a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Swallowing a liquid is the act of taking it down the throat, that is, drinking it.

clue.text: In middle of eclipse in Paris you appeared radiant

indicators.note: placed within, so one piece is set inside the other
only the central portion of the following word is kept

parts.note: the three central letters of eclipse
the familiar French word for you, as said in Paris

explanation.surface: Someone shone brightly during a solar eclipse seen from Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: In Paris signals a French word; there are two ins, the first part of the selector and the second the container.
explanation.definitionFit: When a face lit up it glowed with happiness, so the phrasal verb means looked bright or shining.

clue.text: Cause trouble in prison

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to make mischief between people
second meaning: British slang for jail

explanation.surface: An inmate making mischief behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: Stir is old British slang for prison, as in doing time in stir.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirring means making mischief or provoking conflict, and in slang the same word means a jail.

clue.text: Brief tip for candidates to be interviewed

parts.note: to tip is to lean over, as a ship lists

explanation.surface: Concise advice to job applicants about their interviews.
explanation.walkthrough: Tip looks like advice, but it is the verb meaning lean, as a ship does.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortlist is the reduced set of applicants chosen for final selection, those who get called to interview.

clue.text: Scent unprincipled reversal after departure of Labour leader

indicators.note: the word itself asks for the preceding term to be turned back to front
once something has departed it is gone, so a letter is removed
the one at the head, so only the opening letter of the party name is meant

parts.note: the first letter of the party name

explanation.surface: A whiff of unscrupulous U-turning once the head of the Labour Party has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is Britain's main left-of-centre party; its leader here is just its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a distinctive, usually pleasant smell, so it is a synonym for scent.

clue.text: Be entitled to see very red after reorganisation

indicators.note: once things are reorganised they are in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone has every right to be furious once the office is restructured.
explanation.walkthrough: To see red is to become very angry, which the surface exploits.
explanation.definitionFit: To deserve something is to have earned a right or claim to it, which is being entitled to it.

clue.text: Money to reward workers' time

parts.note: to pay someone is to reward them for work
workers are often called men, as in the boss and his men

explanation.surface: Cash set aside to compensate staff for their hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A payment is a sum of money handed over, so the noun can stand for money paid.
